newsitem.title: THAILAND: Owner to restore fire-hit Bangkok building.
newsitem.headline: Owner to restore fire-hit Bangkok building.

text.p: The owner of the fire-ravaged central Bangkok building from which helicopters plucked more than 93 people said on Monday it would take six months to restore the gutted structure.

Chalermphan Srivikorn also said the 36-storey President Tower building that burned on Sunday, killing three workers, had been insured for 1.7 billion baht ($60 million) with the Nawakij Insurance PLC.
Nawakij said in a separate statement that it would not be affected by the expected damage claim because it had already reinsured the policy with local and foreign firms.
Eight of the 101 workers trapped in the building when it caught fire were admitted to hospital with serious injuries, and others were treated and released.

"The insurance covers only the building and related properties but does not cover the lives of the workers, so the respective contractors have to be responsible for the dead and injured workers," Chalermphan told reporters.
The insurance company and other agencies said they would assess the cost of damage later. Police and the fire officials said investigations into the cause of the fire were continuing.
Some workers told reporters they had heard two blasts on a floor where airconditioning work was going on before the fire broke out.

Sri Dhama Finance Plc said it would temporarily suspend operations because it had been due to open its new office in the President Tower on Monday. The Thai stock exchange suspended the company's shares at its request because the firm is majority owned by the Srivikorn family.
